**Observations:**
- Affected part: leaf (upper surface)
- One prominent lesion near the upper-left of the leaf: circular/oval shape with a white/tan necrotic center and a dark brown-to-black border ring
- The lesion has a distinct "target" or "frog-eye" appearance — pale center surrounded by a dark ring
- Leaf is otherwise green and healthy-looking
- A few smaller dark specks scattered on the leaf
- Background shows yellowing on other leaves (consistent with disease spread in field)

**Reasoning:**
The classic "frog-eye" appearance — a round lesion with a gray/white center and dark reddish-brown to black border — is the hallmark of **Frogeye leaf spot** (*Cercospora sojina*). The lesion here perfectly matches: circular, pale necrotic center, dark distinct margin. This is distinct from Septoria brown spot (irregular brown spots, no pale center) and Cercospora leaf blight (which causes irregular bronzing/purpling on upper canopy leaves rather than discrete circular lesions).
